caseno:
Criminal Misc. Case No. 373 of 1993
and
Criminal Misc. Case No. 400 of 1993
lawyer:
Amirul Kabir Chowdhury, DAG with Syed Abu Kowsar, AAG ----- For the Petitioner in both the cases 
Serajul Huq with KS Nabi and Sharful Islam Khan, Advocates ----- For the Opposite Party in both the cases
parties:
State ----- Petitioner
Vs.
Auranga @ KM Hernayatuddin ----- Opposite Party
full_judgment:
Fazle Hussain Mohammad Habibur Rahman, J.: Criminal Miscellaneous Case No. 373 of 1993 has been heard simultaneously with Criminal Miscellaneous Case No. 400 of 1993 as they arise out of the same Sessions Case No. 300 of 1992 under section 302 of the Penal Code pending in the Court of Mr. Kazi Habibul Awal, Additional Sessions Judge, 8th Court, Dhaka. 

 2. The Rule in Criminal Miscellaneous Case No. 373 of 1993 was issued on 28.2.93 under section 497(5) read with sections 435/439/561A CrPC calling upon the accused-opposite party Auranga @ KM Hemayat Uddin (resident of 111, Free School Street, PS Dhanmondi, District Dhaka) to show cause why the bail allowed to him by order No. 12 dated 22.2.93 passed by the said Additional Sessions Judge, 8th Court, Dhaka in Sessions Case No. 300 of 1992 under section 302 of the Penal Code should not be cancelled or set aside or such other or further order or orders passed as to this Court may seem fit and proper. The operation of the impugned order dated 22.2.93 was stayed till disposal of the Rule. 

 3. In Criminal Misc. Case No. 400 of 1993 Rule was issued on 7.3.93 under section 526(1) CrPC calling upon the accused-opposite party Auranga @ KM Hemayat Uddin to show cause why Sessions Case No. 300 of 1992 pending in the 8th Court of Additional Sessions Judge, Dhaka should not be transferred to any other Court of competent jurisdiction in the Sessions Division at Dhaka or such other or further order or orders passed as to this Court may seem proper. 

 4. The facts of the case are, that on 28.1.80 at 11-00 PM PW 2 Sepoy Fazlul Huq of Defence Forces Intelligence (DFI), Dhaka Cantonment lodged a First Information Report with the Ramna Police Station to the effect that on 28.1.80 at about 6-30 PM he as driver came with an official car to the "New Popular Motor Workshop" behind Hotel Sakura to get the said car repaired there. He saw one person, namely, accused Auranga @ KM Hemayat Uddin entering in to the room of Golam Kibria @ Tipu, the owner of the said workshop. Thereafter he (informant PW 2) saw victim Ali Azam, Naik of DFI coming to the said office of Golam Kibria @ Tipu after the said person, namely, accused Auranga @ KM Hemayat Uddin. After 3/4 minutes that person, namely, accused Auranga @ KM Hemayat Uddin came out of the said room of Golam Kibria @ Tipu and seeing Naik Ali Azam standing there he (accused Auranga) suddenly attacked him (Ali Azam) and throwing him down on the ground sat on his chest and shot him (on the chest from his revolver). Informant PW 2 Sepoy Fazlul Huq saw victim Ali Azam going towards Hotel Sakura with bleeding injury i.e. towards his car and also saw the assailant accused Auranga @ KM Hemayat Uddin fleeing away by back side of the said garage. The companions of Naik Ali Azam (who had not seen the occurrence) in an apparent effort to save his life put him (injured Ali Azam) in the motor vehicle and went towards the Cantonment. At the place of occurrence Golam Kibria @ Tipu the owner of the said workshop and another employee of the said workshop (namely, Swapan) were present. They saw and heard about the occurrence. From them he (PW 2 Fazlul Huq) learnt that the name of the person who shot Ali Azam fatally in his chest is accused Auranga @ KM Hemayat Uddin of Free School Street, PS Dhanmondi, Later he (PW 2) learnt that while victim Ali Azam was being taken towards the Combined Military Hospital, Dhaka Cantonment, he expired on the way near the 3rd gate of the Cantonment. Informant Sepoy Fazlul Huq deposed in the trial Court as PW 2 stating in the trial Court what he had stated in the FIR and he was cross-examined by the defence on the same day i.e. on 23 1.93. PW 2 Fazlul Huq of DGFI identified accused Auranga in the Court as the person who fatally shot Ali Azam by his revolver. It further appears that Golam Kibria @ Tipu, owner of the said New Popular Motor Workshop said in his statement (Ext. 3) under section 164 CrPC to the Magistrate PW 3 Mr. MH Munshi that he knew accused Auranga @ KM Hemayat Uddin from before, that accused Auranga used to come to his motor workshop often, that accused Auranga used to demand "Chanda" (subscription or toll) and often used to take money in that manner from him (by extortion), that on 28.1.80 at about 6-30 PM accused Auranga came to his workshop and demanded Taka 3000.00 as "Chanda", that when he said that he did not have the money, accused Auranga became angry, that he told Auranga that men of NSI, (National Security Intelligence) the Special Branch and other similar agencies (of the Government) often come to look for him, that he should not come to his place any more, that accused Auranga at this stage came out of the room and seeing a person, namely, victim Ali Azam of DFI caught hold of him, threw him down on the ground and sitting on his chest shot him (Ali Azam) by revolver in his chest, that accused Auranga fled away by the back side of his workshop and that injured Ali Azam in bleeding condition ran towards the Sakura Market (i.e. towards his motor car). 

 6. The said accused Auranga remained absconding. Police investigated into the case and submitted charge-sheet on 11.5.81 showing accused Auranga @ KM Hemayat Uddin as absconding. It appears that SI Bhabani Singh submitted the charge-sheet and that in the charge-sheet apart from the seizures of alamats made during the investigation including one fired bullet recovered from the scapula of the deceased, blood stained earth, blood stained seat of Hillman car, etc. he cited as many as 15 witnesses including 3 eye-witnesses, namely, informant PW 2 Sepoy Fazlul Huq, Golam Kibria @ Tipu, owner of the said workshop (resident of 22, Paribagh, PS Ramna), Swapan (son of late Shamsu Ali) who is a mechanic of the said workshop, 2ID, Mymensingh Road, Dhaka and the doctor who held post mortem examination on the dead body of Ali Azam, namely, PW 4 Major (now Lt. Col.) M Motlebur Rahman of Army Medical Corps. Accused Auranga did not surrender and he could not be arrested. On 7.2.80 Golam Kibria @ Tipu's statement under section 164 CrPC was recorded by PW 3 Mr. Md. Mortuza Hossain Munshi, the then Metropolitan Magistrate, Dhaka. In spite of warrant of arrest and proclamation and attachment the arrest of absconding accused Auranga could not be secured. 

 The concerned Magistrate consequently on 7.7.82 filed the case sine die. On 18.8.92 the Police submitted an application before the Chief Metropolitan Magistrate, Dhaka for continuing with the proceedings against the absconding accused Auranga for taking steps for his trial in absentia after complying with the provisions of section 339B CrPC. On 20.8.92 the Chief Metropolitan Magistrate ordered for taking steps in accordance with the provisions of 339B CrPC. On 22.9.92 the Chief Metropolitan Magistrate after observing that proclamation and attachment have been made under sections 67 and 68 CrPC in spite of which accused Auranga was absconding, he directed that the name of accused Auranga be published in two national newspapers for the purpose of his trial in abscontia. Thereafter on 25.10.92 arrested accused Auranga @ KM Hemayat Uddin was produced before the Chief Metropolitan Magistrate who rejected his prayer for bail and sent the case at once to the Court of Sessions for trial. The Sessions Judge, Dhaka received the case record on 26.10.92 from the Court of the Chief Metropolitan Magistrate, took cognizance of the offence against the said accused under section 302 of the Penal Code and at once transferred the case to the Additional Sessions Judge, 8th Court, Dhaka for trial. Mr. Habibul Awal, Additional Sessions Judge, 8th Court, Dhaka received the case record on 27.10.92 and fixed 14.11.92 for production of the accused before the Court and also for hearing regarding the framing of charge against the accused. On 9.11.92 after hearing both the parties the learned Additional Sessions Judge, 8th Court, Dhaka rejected the petition for bail observing that bail cannot be granted to the accused in view of the provision of section 497(1) CrPC. On 14.11.92 charge was framed against accused Auranga @ KM Hemayat Uddin under section 302 of the Penal Code for causing the death of Naik Ali Azam by shooting from a revolver in the chest on 28.1.80 and on the said date i.e. on 14.11.92 the learned Additional Sessions Judge, 8th Court, Dhaka also rejected the petition for bail stating, "A similar petition for bail was rejected on 9.11.92 (in view of the provision of section 497(1) CrPC). I do not find fresh grounds for granting bail to the accused. The petition for bail is, therefore, rejected". He fixed 7.1.93 for trial of the accused issuing the bailable warrants for all the witnesses. On 7.1.93 accused Auranga @ KM Hemayat Uddin was brought to theCourt but no prosecution witness was brought except one Md. Fazlur Rahman who was not cited in the charge-sheet and witness warrant was served on him wrongly. The police could not serve the witness warrants on any other prosecution witness. Thereafter the case was adjourned to 23.1.93 for examination of 4 witnesses, namely, Fazlul Huq, Golam Kibria @ Tipu, Swapan and Sk. Kamruzzaman. On 23.1.93 one formal witness PW 1 Kazi Emdadul Huq (a duty officer who recorded the FIR) and eye-witness informant PW 2 Sepoy Md. Fazlul Huq of DFI were examined and cross-examined by the defence on the same day. The learned Additional Sessions Judge observed that return of service of witness warrants on two material witnesses such as Golam Kibria @ Tipu and Swapan were not received in the Court. The learned Additional Sessions Judge fixed 20.2.93 for examination of witnesses directing issuance of witness warrants against all the remaining witnesses. On 20.2.93 PW 3 Mr. Mortuza Hossain Munshi, the then Metropolitan Magistrate (who recorded the statement Ext. 3 of eye-witness Golam Kibria @ Tipu under section 164 CrPC), PW 4 Lt. Col. Motlebur Rahman who held post mortem examination on the dead body of Naik Ali Azam, PW 5 Lt. Col. Abdur Rashid Howlader (witness of the inquest) were examined and cross-examined by the defence. Thereafter the Additional Sessions Judge adjourned the case for about six weeks fixing 4.4 93, 5.4.93, 6.4.93 and 7.4.93 for further trial issuing witness warrants for the rest of the witnesses but curiously abruptly fixed 22.2.93 for order on the bail petition filed by the accused on 20.2.93. On 22.2.93 the learned Additional Sessions Judge Mr. Kazi Habibul Awal passed the impugned order No. 12 dated 22.2.93 stating that accused Auranga @ KM Hemayat Uddin is a member of the Parliament, that on 14.11.92 the charge against him (under section 302 of the Penal Code for committing the murder of Naik Ali Azam was framed against him) was framed, that on issuance of witness warrants 7.1.93 was fixed for examination of witnesses, that on 7.1.93 no witness turned up, that on the next date 23.1.93 which was fixed for examination of witnesses 3 witnesses filed hajira, that on the said date 23.1.93 PW 1 Kazi Emdadul Huq, Duty Officer of Ramna Ps who filled up the FIR form and informant PW 2 Md. Fazlul Huq of DGFI were examined., that the 3rd witness who had filed hajira was not examined on the advice of the public prosecutor, that on 20.2.93 which was fixed for examination of further witnesses 3 more namely, PW 3 Mr. MH Munshi, the then Metropolitan Magistrate (who proved the statement Ext. 3 of Golam Kibria @ Tipu recorded under section 164 CrPC), PW 4 Dr. Lt. Col. M Motlebur Rahman who proved the post mortem report and stated what he found on making the post mortem examination on the dead body of Naik Ali Azam and PW 5 Li Col. Abdur Rashid (a witness of inquest) were examined, that two important witnesses, namely, Golam Kibira @ Tipu and Swapan have not yet been examined, that they are said to have seen the commission of the murder, that without their evidence it will be difficult or almost impossible to make objective findings upon the facts in issue so as to ascertain the criminal liability of the accused, that it is uncertain when the said two witnesses Golam Kibira @ Tipu and Swapan will be examined, that the alleged crime was committed by the accused Hemayat Uddin @ Auranga on 28.1.80, that as the said accused was absconding, the Metropolitan Magistrate was justified in filing the case sine die as there was no provision for trial of the accused in absentia at that time, that when the provision for trial of the accused in absentia was inserted in the Code of Criminal Procedure by amendment, the trial of the absconding accused could have been started and completed earlier, that the delay in starting the trial of the accused in spite of the provision of section 339B CrPC is an act of irresponsibility on the part of the concerned Government agencies, that it is not illegal to start the trial at this stage after the arrest of the accused, since there is no time limit with respect to the criminal proceedings, that section 344 CrPC empowers the Court to allow adjournments of a case when considered necessary, that the case was adjourned for 45 days to enable the prosecution to secure the attendance of the vital witnesses of the present case, that under the provision of "section 497 CrPC the case is not generally bailable if the Court feels that the accused is guilty of an offence punishable with death or imprisonment for life", that the accused having been charged under section 302 of the Penal Code should not be granted bail in view of the provision of section 497(1) CrPC and that But for reason that the State has failed to produce the vital eye-witnesses as yet (the trial Judge does not strangely state a word about the examination of eye-witness informant PW 2) and for the reason that I have been informed that those witnesses are now abroad and there is no certainty about their attendance in the Court, now I am in a position to entertain doubt as to whether the State will succeed in proving this case against the accused with sufficient positive legal evidence. For such reason and for other reasons stated already herein above, the accused deserves to be admitted to bail. I must not be understood to mean that I have formed an opinion in favour or against the alleged criminal liability of the accused-petitioner. I mean to say that the State should produce more evidence and till then the accused should enjoy the facility of enlargement of bail………..Accused-Petitioner Auranga @ KM Hemayat Uddin, MP be admitted to the bail of his brother, a Deputy General Manager of Janata Bank as his security of Taka 1,00,000.00." 

 8. Mr. KS Nabi, the learned Advocate for the accused-opposite party strangely argues that as under sub-section (5) of section 497 CrPC the High Court Division and the Court of Sessions have concurrent jurisdiction to cause arrest of the accused released on bail and to commit him to custody, the Court of Sessions is not inferior to the High Court Division and this Court has no jurisdiction to cancel or set aside the order of bail passed by the learned Additional Sessions Judge. There is no substance whatsoever in this argument. In the instant case the accused-opposite party was granted bail, but before he was released on bail this Court stayed the impugned order granting bail to the accused and, as already stated, the accused-opposite party is also in jail custody as a detenu under section 3 of the Special Powers Act. Therefore, sub-section (5) of section 497 CrPC does not come into play at all in the instant case. For the reasons stated below, this Court has power to cancel the bail accused was granted by the Additional Sessions Judge even if section 497 (5) CrPC is attracted. In the case of Md. Shahabuddin Vs The State and Azam Khan, 37 DLR 196 a Division Bench of this Court set aside the order of the learned Sessions Judge, Dhaka granting bail to accused Azam Khan for two days as he was being tried for committing the offence of murder on being charged under section 302 of the Penal Code. Section 439 read with section 435 of the Code of Criminal Procedure has clearly empowered the High Court Division, in its discretion, to exercise any of the powers conferred on a Court of appeal by sections 423, 427 and 428, etc. of the CrPC in revision against any order of any inferior Court and section 423(1)(c) CrPC empowers this Court to alter or reverse any order passed by the inferior Court. The term "inferior" has been interpreted to mean "judicially inferior", i.e. a Court over which the Court proceeding under section 435 CrPC has appellate jurisdiction (See Nobin Vs. Russick, ILR 10 CaL 268). It carries with it the idea of subordination which means "inferiority in rank" (See Priya Gopal, lLR 9 Bom. 100). Inferior Criminal Court only means judicially inferior to the High Court Division and it is well-settled that a Court is undoubtedly inferior to another Court, when an appeal lies from the former to the latter. It is, therefore, beyond any question that this Court has revisional jurisdiction under sections 439 and 561A CrPC against the aforesaid impugned order passed by the learned Additional Sessions Judge. 

 9. Since the accused-opposite party is not under the age of 16 years or any woman or any sick or infirm person, he cannot be released on bail if there appear reasonable grounds for believing that he has been guilty of an offence punishable with death or imprisonment for life. The fact that the accused has become a member of the Parliament is no ground at all for releasing him on bail since his case does not come within the purview of the proviso to the aforesaid section 497(1) CrPC. It is needless to state that all are equal in the eye of law. Extraordinary delay and inordinate procrastination in disposing of a case may be under certain circumstances a ground for ball of the accused; but in the instant case the accused-opposite party was absconding right from the inception of the case and his arrest could not be secured. Lastly, when steps were being taken by the Metropolitan Magistrate concerned for getting him tried in absentia by publishing his name in two national daily newspapers as required under section 339B CrPC the police was successful in securing the arrest of accused-opposite party on 25.10.92. The case record was at once sent to the Sessions Judge, Dhaka on 26.10.92 who took cognizance of the case of the offence under section 302 of the Penal Code against the accused-opposite party. The case was transferred by the Sessions Judge, Dhaka on that very day to the 8th Court of Additional Sessions Judge, Dhaka. On receipt of the case record learned Additional Sessions Judge on 27.10.92 fixed 31.10.92 for hearing and after refusing prayer for bail of the accused-opposite party on two occasions as aforesaid, ultimately framed charge under section 302 of the Penal Code on 14.11.92. Apart from the statement Ext. 3 of Golam Kibria recorded by the Magistrate PW 3 under section 164 CrPC the learned Additional Sessions Judge had before him the direct ocular evidence of a very vital witness, namely, informant PW 2 Fazlul Huq of the DFI who identified the accused-opposite party as the person who in his presence fired the fatal shot of revolver in the chest of deceased Ali Azam on the date of occurrence at the aforesaid time and place of occurrence which the learned Additional Sessions Judge curiously enough conveniently omitted to mention in the impugned order. The evidence of PW 2 informant Fazlul Huq is alone sufficient to hold in terms of section 497(1) CrPC that there are reasonable grounds for believing that the accused- opposite party has been guilty of an offence punishable under section 302 of the Penal Code with death or imprisonment for life. Further after the abolition of the commitment proceedings, section 205C( c) has been inserted in the Code of Criminal Procedure providing that when in a case instituted on a police report the accused appears or is brought before the Magistrate and it appears to the Magistrate that the offence is triable exclusively by the Court of Sessions, he shall send the case to the Court of Sessions and send to the Court of Sessions the record of the case and the documents and articles, if any, which are to be produced in evidence. The documents obviously mean-and include the FIR, the charge-sheet and the statements recorded under sections 161 and 164 CrPC. In pursuance of the provisions of section 265D CrPC upon consideration of the record of the case and the documents submitted therewith and after hearing both the parties the learned Additional Sessions Judge had no other alternative but to hold the opinion that there are sufficient grounds for believing that the accused has committed the offence of murdering Ali Azam and consequently framed charge against the accused-opposite party under section 302 of the Penal Code. Keeping in view the evidence of informant PW 2 Fazlul Huq and the statements of Golam Kibria @ Tipu and Swapan under sections 164 and 161 CrPC respectively (which are documents on record within the meaning of section 265D CrPC) (See Abdul Motalib and others Vs. the State, 27 DLR 665) it cannot be said in the instant case that there appear no reasonable grounds for believing that the accused opposite party has been guilty of an offence which is punishable under section 302 of the Penal Code with death or imprisonment for life. The learned Additional Sessions Judge fixed 7.1.93 as the first date for examination of the prosecution witnesses and on 23.1.93 he examined 2 witnesses and thereafter on 20.2.93 he examined 3 more witnesses. It is curious that although from .7.1.93 to 20.2.93 when only about six weeks had elapsed the learned Additional Sessions Judge made following unwarranted observation in granting bail to the accused: 

 "…………..there is no certainty about their attendance in the Court, now I am in a position to entertain doubtas to whether the State will succeed in proving this .case against the accused-petitioner with sufficient positive legal evidence. For such reason and for other reasons stated already hereinabove, the accused deserves to be admitted to bail." 

 It seems he has taken no notice of the fact that a Sessions Judge, an Additional Sessions Judge or an Assistant Sessions Judge under the newly amended section 339C(2) CrPC is required to conclude the trial of a case within 360 working days from the date on which the case is received by him for trial. As there are sufficient reasonable grounds for believing that the accused-opposite party has been guilty of committing the offence of murder punishable under section 302 of the Penal Code with death or imprisonment for life and as the case does not come within the purview of the proviso to section 497(1) CrPC, there is absolutely no ground on which the accused-opposite party can be released on bail. We do not find that there was any unnecessary procrastination or delay in prosecuting the accused in view of the fact that the accused-opposite party himself absconded for a long time till 25.10.92 after commission of the offence on 28.1.80 due to which the charge against him under section 302 of the Penal Code could be framed only on 14.11.92. In these circumstances we are of the view that the learned Additional Sessions Judge had no jurisdiction whatsoever to grant bail to the accused-opposite party. The impugned order No. 12 dated 22.2.93, therefore, must be set aside. 

 10. Now the question is, whether the instant case should be allowed to be tried by the learned Additional Sessions Judge Mr. Kazi Habibul Awal or should be transferred to any other Court of competent jurisdiction. In view of the fact that the said learned Additional Sessions Judge has already observed that he entertains doubt as to whether the State will succeed in proving this case against the accused-opposite party with sufficient positive legal evidence, the State has every reason to feel and think there will be no fair trial in the said Court as the Court has already become biased. It is also said by the prosecution that the accused is personally known to the trial Judge from before (i.e. from the student days). Justice must not only be done, but must also be seen to have been done. In these circumstances we are of the view that the case should be transferred to some other Court of competent jurisdiction. 

 11. In the result, the Rules are made absolute. The impugned order No. 12 dated 22.2.93 passed by the learned Additional Sessions Judge, 8th Court, Dhaka in Sessions Case No. 300 of 1992 granting bail to accused Auranga @ KM Hemayat Uddin is set aside. The said Sessions Case No. 300 of 1992 is withdrawn from the Court of Additional Sessions Judge, 8th Court. Dhaka and transferred to the Court of Sessions Judge, Dhaka for trial by himself. The learned Sessions Judge, Dhaka is directed to complete the trial and dispose of the case as expeditiously as possible in accordance with law.
